Tip1: The ADNIMERGE file (ADNIMERGE - Key ADNI tables merged into one table [ADNI1,GO,2,3]) may be of interest, as it combines various variables into one file.
Tip2: Downloading MRI images from IDA can be difficult due to the large number of files per subject. A practical approach is to use the Advanced Search with top-level filters like anat T1w MRI and generate an image collection. Download the resulting CSV file, open it in Excel, and inspect the series descriptions to identify the specific T1w scans you need (e.g., MPRAGE). Use these refined descriptions to filter the dataset again in the Advanced Download section, then add the correct images to your download queue and use the IDA Downloader to retrieve them.

Research_Article_1_Title: Distortion correction of diffusion weighted MRI without reverse phase-encoding scans or field-maps
Research_Article_1_Description: Introduces a deep learning approach to synthesize geometrically accurate b0 images from structural T1w and diffusion MRI data, enabling susceptibility distortion correction without requiring reverse phase encoding scans and achieves performance comparable to traditional techniques like FSL topup.

Description: Part of the Amsterdam Open MRI Collection, this dataset includes multimodal MRI data from 1,000 participants, focusing on individual differences.
Research_Article_1_Title: Self-Supervised Learning of Brain Dynamics from Broad Neuroimaging Data
Research_Article_1_Description: Proposed self-supervised learning frameworks for neuroimaging data, inspired by NLP. At their core, these frameworks learn the dynamics of brain activity by modeling sequences of activity akin to how sequences of text are modeled in NLP. We evaluate the frameworks by pre-training models on a broad neuroimaging dataset spanning functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging data
Research_Article_2_Title: Is political ideology correlated with brain structure? A preregistered replication
Research_Article_2_Description: Studies the hypotheses that conservatism positively correlates with amygdala and negatively with anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) gray matter volume. This is the largest preregistered replication study in the context of political neuroscience. Confirmatory tests highlight weak, positive associations between the right fusiform gyri and conservatism

Research_Article_1_Title: Brain asymmetry is globally different in males and females: exploring cortical volume, area, thickness, and mean curvature
Research_Article_1_Description: This study investigate sexual dimorphism in brain asymmetry by comparing laterality index with the distance index, which is a global measure of differences within and across hemispheres, and with the subtraction index, which compares pairwise raw values in the left and right hemisphere. Machine learning models, robustness tests, and group analyses of cortical volume, area, thickness, and mean curvature revealed that, of the three indices, distance index was the most successful biomarker of sexual dimorphism.

Description: A large-scale neuroimaging dataset developed by Harvard and MGH, the BGSP includes structural and functional MRI data from over 1,500 healthy young adults, along with behavioral, cognitive, and genetic information.
Research_Article_1_Title: Accurate nonlinear mapping between MNI volumetric and FreeSurfer surface coordinate systems
Research_Article_1_Description: Mapping between volumetric (e.g., MNI152) and surface (e.g., fsaverage) coordinate systems is crucial for neuroimaging, but methods for accurate transformations are underexplored. This research leverages the BGSP data to evaluate three approaches for this mapping, simulating the projection of group data and parcellations between these systems.

Description: A longitudinal study based in Brazil aiming to understand the development of mental disorders in children and adolescents.
Research_Article_1_Title: Estimated Prevalence of Depressive Disorders in Children From 2004 to 2019 A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Research_Article_1_Description: Depression during childhood (ie, age <13 years) poses a major health burden. Recent changes in environmental and lifestyle factors may increase children’s risk of mental health problems. This has been reported for anxiety disorders, but it is unclear whether this occurs for depressive disorders.
Research_Article_2_Title: Early Adversity and Development: Parsing Heterogeneity and Identifying Pathways of Risk and Resilience
Research_Article_2_Description: This research highlights how distinct adversity types (threat vs. deprivation) during development differentially impact psychopathology-threat affecting emotional processing via attention biases and genetic markers (e.g., *NR3C1*), while deprivation disrupts executive function through cortical-striatal circuits. Longitudinal data and multi-modal assessments revealed outcome heterogeneity tied to adversity timing, type, and protective factors, informing targeted intervention strategies.

Description: The BrainLat Project is a comprehensive, open-access neuroimaging dataset developed by the Latin American Brain Health Institute (BrainLat) to advance research on neurodegenerative diseases within underrepresented populations. It encompasses multimodal data from 780 participants across five Latin American countries: Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, and Peru.​
Research_Article_1_Title: Brain clocks capture diversity and disparities in aging and dementia across geographically diverse populations
Research_Article_1_Description: Region-specific analysis of accelerated brain aging by providing multimodal neuroimaging (fMRI/EEG) and clinical data from underrepresented Latin American populations, capturing structural inequality’s impact via frontoposterior network disruptions and sex-specific gaps linked to macrosocial stressors. Its inclusion of diverse sociodemographic, environmental, and genetic admixture profiles supported models where socioeconomic disparities and pollution explained 37% of variance in brain-age gaps, highlighting Global South vulnerabilities to accelerated neurodegeneration
Research_Article_2_Title: Altered spatiotemporal brain dynamics of interoception in behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia
Research_Article_2_Description: The study revealed that behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients exhibit prolonged intrinsic neural timescales during interoception, measured via EEG autocorrelation windows, linking these dynamic deficits to structural atrophy in fronto-insular-temporal regions and sociocognitive impairments. Multimodal data-including simultaneous EEG/ECG, structural MRI, and neuropsychological assessments-enabled mapping of spatiotemporal brain dynamics to allostatic-interoceptive network degradation, establishing a mechanistic basis for bvFTD’s behavioral symptoms

Research_Article_1_Title: Recurrent Variational Network: A Deep Learning Inverse Problem Solver applied to the task of Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
Research_Article_1_Description: Conventional MRI acquisition is slow and prone to motion artifacts, limiting dynamic treatments. A novel deep learning method, RecurrentVarNet, reconstructs high-fidelity MRI images from highly accelerated, subsampled data by iteratively refining k-space using recurrent neural networks, achieving state-of-the-art results on brain data.
Research_Article_2_Title: AI-Based Reconstruction for Fast MRI—A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Research_Article_2_Description: Deep learning and compressed sensing are increasingly combined to accelerate MRI acquisition, leading to significant advancements. This meta-analysis reviews these deep-learning-based CS techniques, their designs, breakthroughs, and future directions, while also providing a framework for their assessment in fast MRI.
